To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the performance of a hypothetical system can be substantially improved by using the right classifier and inference procedures, and (b) the accuracy and privacy impacts of such systems depend on the data and on the classifier.

(1) the accuracy of a data mining system can be substantially improved by using a more complex classifier, (2) the accuracy of the system can be further improved by using a larger training sample, (3) the accuracy of such a system can be further substantially improved by applying the data mining system to a larger data set, and (4) the privacy of the individuals in the training sample can be substantially reduced if the data mining system uses a complex classifier.

the accuracy and privacy impacts of data mining systems can be significantly reduced by the following: (1) using more accurate and more relevant data, (2) using more accurate classifiers, (3) using more accurate inference rules, and (4) using a more accurate overall system architecture.

the question: "What is the best we can do, technically, to achieve the goals of information awareness while protecting privacy?"
the technical design space for data mining systems, not with any specific system concept.

a more nuanced and realistic understanding of data mining systems is necessary to assess the accuracy of their predictions and the privacy impact of their operation.
